referees.quote: we would support publication in Nature Communications in broad terms, however we have several questions about the overall basic interpretation of the data
Before recommending for publication, I believe the authors should address a few outstanding issues identified below.
In my opinion, the paper shows limited amount of novelties for a Nature journal... If further understanding would be gained about this point I would reconsider my opinion.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

note: Round 1 is Version 0; no transfer from another journal is indicated. R1: major revision because they asked for a new quantitative dataset for gate geometry G2/3 and a detailed reconciliation of Fig. 3a with Fig. 3b. R2: requests are mostly clarifications and added discussion (laser invasiveness, r0 extraction, error bars, labeling), not new data, so minor revision; this could arguably be major. R3: reject because they cited insufficient novelty for the journal, though they left the door open to reconsider. R4 is an early-career co-reviewer who submitted no independent report and did not say which report they co-signed. R1's report is written in the plural ('we would support', 'To the best of our knowledge'), so R4 is assumed to be R1's co-reviewer and given R1's recommendation; this pairing is an inference. A separate editorial comment from an invited peer who did not file a full report (on gate-polarity and electron/hole injection) is not counted as a referee.
